correctness.rationale: For all \(m\ge1\), a first/last-difference deletion-alignment argument forces complementary central alternating intervals. This proves the exact edge criterion, even-length edgelessness, and the odd-length rooted binomial-tree recursion. A last-bit perfect matching and tree bipartition give independence number \(2^{m-1}\). The maximum-codebook recurrence and product follow by induction; direct shadow checks corroborate \(1\le m\le8\) and brute-force codebooks verify \(1\le m\le4\).

value.rationale: A natural reversal-constrained code family under the standard one-deletion synchronization channel has an exact infinite classification. The explicit tree isomorphism explains the sharp odd/even split and the optimizer count; the parameter is the full code family, not an arbitrary finite slice. It connects constrained code design and binomial-tree combinatorics without claiming new abstract tree enumeration or biochemical utility.
